def: A program with more than one agent loop, each with its own context, in which the output of one agent becomes input to another.
The orchestrating agent in a manager design that plans the work, writes briefs, delegates to sub-agents and synthesises their results.
An agent loop started by a lead agent for one part of a task, working in its own fresh context and returning a condensed result.
A multi-agent design in which a central agent calls specialised agents as tools and keeps control of the plan and the final answer.
A one-way transfer in which one agent passes execution and the conversation state to another agent that takes over.
Giving a sub-agent its own clean window so that search results and dead ends stay out of the lead's context, which receives only a summary.
The instruction a lead gives a sub-agent, stating an objective, output format, guidance on tools and sources, and clear task boundaries.
A choice such as a style, format or name that an agent makes while acting and that parallel agents cannot see, causing conflicts when merged.
A design rule in which several agents may contribute research or review but only one agent edits the shared artefact, avoiding conflicting writes.
A category of multi-agent failure in which agents fail to communicate, share or act on what another agent produced.
A limit on sub-agent count, depth, steps, tokens or wall-clock time that is enforced in code rather than requested in a prompt.
